1	# Project brief
2	
3	## Purpose
4	
5	Carrylog gives a repository one durable project-context and handoff layer shared by multiple AI coding
6	agents. Canonical Markdown stays human-reviewable; deterministic adapters route Codex, Claude Code,
7	and future tools to the right context without copied sources drifting. Durable truth belongs to the
8	repository rather than a model session or machine-local journal.
9	
10	## Users
11	
12	- Developers who switch among AI coding agents or machines on the same repository.
13	- Teams that need reviewable architecture, quality, decision, and handoff constraints in Git.
14	- Maintainers who want context changes reviewed and versioned with code.
15	
16	## In scope
17	
18	- Local-first context structure and versioned schema.
19	- Progressive always/on-demand loading.
20	- Non-destructive instruction-file adapters.
21	- Verifiable handoff evidence and drift/freshness checks.
22	- Cross-platform CLI, CI automation, and later opt-in skills/MCP access.
23	
24	## Non-goals
25	
26	- A complete software-development methodology or agent orchestrator.
27	- Replacing Git, issue trackers, ADRs, product documentation, or automatic session journals.
28	- Hidden LLM calls in deterministic validation.
29	- Uploading repository context or telemetry by default.
30	- Claiming semantic freshness when only file structure was validated.
31	
32	Detailed scope and success criteria live in `docs/product-scope.md`.
33

1	# Context operating rules
2	
3	## At the start of work
4	
5	1. Read every document marked `load: always` in `config.yaml`.
6	2. Load on-demand documents only when their descriptions or triggers match the task.
7	3. Compare the requested work, the repository state, and this context before editing.
8	4. Report consequential mismatches before relying on stale context.
9	
10	## While working
11	
12	- Treat source code and executable tests as evidence, not as substitutes for product intent.
13	- Keep changes inside the requested scope and record decisions that constrain future work.
14	- Do not silently rewrite human-authored content outside generated adapter blocks.
15	
16	## Before handing off
17	
18	- Update `current-state.md` when implementation status or priorities changed.
19	- Update `handoff.md` with verified changes, checks run, unresolved risks, and the next best task.
20	- Add or link a decision record when a consequential design choice was made.
21	- Run `carrylog validate` and the project's relevant quality checks.

1	# Engineering conventions
2	
3	## Supported environments
4	
5	- Node.js 22 and 24.
6	- Linux, macOS, and Windows are the supported beta matrix.
7	- TypeScript uses strict unchecked-index and exact-optional-property checks.
8	
9	## Commands
10	
11	```bash
12	npm ci
13	npm run build
14	npm run format:check
15	npm run check
16	npm test
17	npm run test:coverage
18	npm run quality
19	npm run pack:check
20	npm run test:package
21	node dist/cli.js sync --check
22	node dist/cli.js validate --json
23	```
24	
25	When shell commands are run in this repository's current Codex environment, prefix every command
26	segment with `rtk` as required by the root AGENTS instructions.
27	
28	## Change quality
29	
30	- Fix root causes rather than adding repository-specific exceptions.
31	- Keep mutation in commands and safe filesystem utilities; renderers stay pure.
32	- Add regression coverage for defects and both accepted/rejected cases for safety changes.
33	- Record schema, compatibility, dependency, or architectural choices as ADRs.
34	- Update product docs, current state, engineering log, and handoff when materially affected.
35	- Do not claim checks that were not run.
36	
37	Large beta changes require a dedicated review pass with findings recorded and resolved or accepted.
38	Tagged releases additionally require `npm run release:verify`, a clean licensed commit, and the
39	protected workflow in `docs/releasing.md`.

5	export function hasContinuitySkillMarker(content: string): boolean {
6	  const normalized = content.replace(/\r\n?/g, "\n");
7	  return normalized.split("\n").filter((line) => line === CONTINUITY_SKILL_MARKER).length === 1;

10	export function renderAgentContinuitySkill(): string {
11	  return `---
12	name: carrylog-continuity
13	description: Resume work from Carrylog or leave a verified checkpoint when continuing across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI.
14	---
15	
16	${CONTINUITY_SKILL_MARKER}
17	
18	# Carrylog continuity
19	
20	Use this workflow only when the user asks to resume, continue, checkpoint, hand off, or end a
21	substantial project session.
22	
23	## Resume
24	
25	1. Resolve one offline executable before running resume, in this order:
26	   a. In the Carrylog source repository itself, when its built \`dist/cli.js\` exists, first require
27	      \`node dist/cli.js resume --help\` to succeed, then use \`node dist/cli.js resume --json\` from
28	      that repository root. If it fails, report a stale or incompatible build and stop.
29	   b. Otherwise, when the nearest project has \`node_modules/.bin/carrylog\`, first require
30	      \`npx --no-install carrylog resume --help\` to succeed, then run
31	      \`npx --no-install carrylog resume --json\` from that project root. If it fails, report the
32	      incompatible pinned version and stop; do not fall through to a different global version.
33	   c. Otherwise, use a global \`carrylog\` only after \`carrylog resume --help\` succeeds; then run
34	      \`carrylog resume --json\`.
35	   Never select a global executable before checking the source and project-pinned candidates. If a
36	   selected version lacks \`resume\`, report the incompatible version and require an explicit build,
37	   project install, or upgrade. Never download, build, or upgrade Carrylog automatically.
38	2. Read the always-context and checkpoint in the envelope.
39	3. Load only on-demand documents whose triggers match the task.
40	4. Compare the checkpoint, repository, and requested work. Report material mismatches before editing.
41	5. Summarize the objective, verified state, next action, and risks, then continue the requested work.
42	
43	## Checkpoint
44	
45	1. Update the configured current-state and checkpoint documents using verified facts only.
46	2. Record consequential architecture or dependency decisions in the project's decision records.
47	3. Keep these checkpoint sections exactly once and in order: Objective, Completed, Verification,
48	   Decisions, Risks, Next action.
49	4. Run \`carrylog checkpoint\`, then \`carrylog validate\` and the relevant project checks, using the
50	   same offline executable resolution as resume.
51	5. Never persist raw transcripts, hidden reasoning, credentials, or unreviewed tool output.
52	`;
53	}

775	surfaces allowed terminal controls, bidirectional formatting, or multiline field spoofing from
776	repository-controlled Markdown, paths, and Git evidence. Human fields and diagnostics now escape

783	handoff with generated evidence now migrates in LF and CRLF while preserving that evidence; direct v1
